_doc: Optional modernizations: things the code does today that the client could do with a managed AWS service instead. NONE of them is needed to run on Linux or AWS, so they are reported separately and never added to the estimate total. Each item: detect = regexes matched against C# / VB / config source lines; aws = suggested service; hours = manual-equivalent coding hours [fixed low, fixed high] plus per_file for each additional file using it; hours are multiplied by the AI code factor like any other coding work. Add items here, not in code.

items.title: SMTP email
items.aws: Amazon SES (SDK or SMTP interface); optionally add SMS notifications with Amazon SNS
items.why: Removes the need to keep an SMTP relay reachable from AWS, adds delivery metrics, bounce handling and per-message cost visibility.

items.title: SMS gateway client
items.aws: Amazon SNS (SMS) or AWS End User Messaging
items.why: Replaces a third-party SMS vendor SDK with a managed AWS service when consolidating vendors or billing.

items.title: Kafka producer / consumer
items.aws: Amazon SQS + SNS (queues, fan-out) or Amazon EventBridge; keep Kafka semantics with Amazon MSK when ordered replay is required
items.why: A self-managed Kafka cluster is the biggest operational cost behind simple queueing; SQS/SNS remove it when ordered replay and long retention are not used.

items.title: Message queue (RabbitMQ, ActiveMQ, MSMQ, NServiceBus, MassTransit)
items.aws: Amazon SQS + SNS, or Amazon MQ to keep the broker protocol
items.why: MSMQ cannot run on Linux at all (a required finding elsewhere); for the others a managed broker removes patching and capacity work.

items.title: Local or network file storage
items.aws: Amazon S3 (pre-signed URLs for downloads and uploads)
items.why: Local disk and file shares do not scale out and are lost when a container restarts; S3 gives durability and removes the share dependency.

items.title: In-process cache or session state
items.why: Needed once the application runs on more than one instance; until then an in-process cache is fine.

items.title: In-app scheduler or timer jobs
items.aws: Amazon EventBridge Scheduler triggering an ECS task or Lambda
items.why: In-process schedulers run once per instance when scaled out and need a database for coordination; a managed scheduler runs each job once.

items.title: Forms / Windows / ASP.NET Identity authentication
items.aws: Amazon Cognito or AWS IAM Identity Center with OpenID Connect
items.why: Windows authentication does not work from Linux without extra set-up; a managed OIDC provider also gives SSO, MFA and no password storage.

items.title: File or Event Log logging
items.aws: Serilog / ILogger with a CloudWatch Logs or OpenTelemetry sink
items.why: Containers should write to stdout and have logs collected centrally; Windows Event Log does not exist on Linux (required finding elsewhere).

items.title: Self-hosted search (Lucene, Solr, Elasticsearch)
items.why: Removes cluster patching and capacity planning for search.
